# netris_vpc

Netris enables the creation and management of multiple isolated Virtual Private Clouds (VPCs) within a single hardware infrastructure. Each Netris VPC runs an isolated virtual routing and forwarding table (VRF) with BGP, static routing, and looking glass (centralized routing table lookup) support. Netris VPCs also provide isolated IPAM and V-Net (Layer2 with default gateway).

## Example Usages

```hcl
resource "netris_vpc" "my-vpc" {
   name = "my-vpc"
   tenantid = netris_tenant.my-tenant.id
   guesttenantid {
     id = data.netris_tenant.admin.id
   }
   vni = "auto"
   importrt {
     target { value = "65000:100" }
   }
   # tags = ["foo", "bar"]
 }
```


<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- **name** (String) User assigned name of VPC.
- **tenantid** (Number) ID of tenant. Users of this tenant will be permitted to edit this unit.


### Optional

- **vni** (String) L3VNI: `"auto"` or a number from `1` to `16777215`. Omitted on create allocates automatically.
- **importrt**, **exportrt** (Block List, max 1) Custom route targets for each direction. Controller-generated default and peering targets are preserved. Omit the block to leave that direction unmanaged; an empty block (for example, `exportrt {}`) removes its custom targets. Requires Controller 4.21 or later, as does `vni`. (see [below](#nestedblock--route-targets))
- **guesttenantid** (Block List) Tenant allowed to add/remove services to the VPC but not allowed to manage other parameters of it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--guesttenantid))
- **tags** (List of String) List of tags. Example `["foo", "bar"]`


### Read-Only

- **vrfname** (String) VRF name supplied by the controller; useful for external RADIUS VRF assignment.

<a id="nestedblock--guesttenantid"></a>
### Nested Schema for `guesttenantid`

Required:

- **id** (Number) The ID of a guest tenant who is authorized to add/remove services to the VPC but not allowed to manage other parameters of it.

<a id="nestedblock--route-targets"></a>
### Nested Schema for `importrt` and `exportrt`

- **target** (Block List) Route-target entries. Keep a custom entry in place when editing its value to preserve its ID.
- **target.value** (String, required) `ASN:number` or `IPv4:number`. Values must be unique within each direction.
- **target.id** (Number, read-only) Controller-assigned route-target ID.
- **target.type** (String, read-only) `default-RT`, `vpc-peering-RT`, or `custom-RT`.

On manual VNI creation, each managed direction preserves one default per distinct Site `defaultrtasn`. With no Sites, it uses `65000`; a nonempty response without this field uses legacy `0`. A mix of present and absent fields fails before creation. An empty response cannot identify an older controller's default.

A value matching a generated target refers to the existing row; removing or changing that entry does not delete or edit the generated row. Omit the generated default target from these blocks when changing `vni`.

If changing `vni` also removes or edits a custom target that could become the new default, apply that target change first, then change `vni`.

After import, configured RT blocks are adopted on the next apply. Removing a block may show its entries being removed in the plan, but only stops managing that direction; it does not delete the controller's targets. The VPC data source returns all route targets.
